engine.title: The multibagger screen qualified nobody for four weeks
engine.body: Corrects what this entry said on 2026-08-27. It read ‘the scan is running on schedule’ and blamed the fixed list on cadence. The ledger says otherwise: the last multibagger row is 2026-08-01, while magic, magicmagic and ai_longterm — the same Saturday job, the same slot — all logged 2026-08-22. Twenty-six days, three Saturdays, nothing written.
engine.note: The screen is not broken. Run on 2026-08-27 it took 11 candidates and rejected 10 for R:R below 2.0 — CHENNPETRO 1.29, FLUOROCHEM 1.07, GLAXO 0.59, which needs a 63% win rate merely to break even. The defect was that a week qualifying nobody wrote nothing at all, so the page served the 1 August list as though it were current. The attempt is recorded either way now. The gate is NOT loosened: publishing a 0.59 R:R to keep the section busy is the exact trade this screen exists to refuse, and an empty week is a real result.

engine.title: Stop buying strength that has already run
engine.body: The 4H RSI ceiling for longs was 75. Splitting every closed trade by the RSI recorded at entry showed the engine bleeding above 65 and profitable below it. The ceiling is now 65.
engine.note: Holds in both halves of the sample and at every cut point tested (60, 65, 70), so it is not one lucky threshold. The threshold was still chosen from this sample, so treat the size as an upper bound.

engine.title: A break-even stop would not have helped
engine.body: The median losing trade was +1.44R in profit before it reversed, and 59% touched a full +1R first. That looks like an obvious fix: move the stop to entry once price pays 1R. Re-walking every trade bar by bar, with winners subject to the same rule, says otherwise.
engine.note: The first version of this test only altered losers, which guarantees a positive answer. Correcting it reversed the conclusion. Nothing tested cleared one standard error, so no stop rule was adopted.

engine.title: Trades were being closed at prices that never traded
engine.body: The grader had never resolved a single trade — an exception was being swallowed silently — leaving a fallback path that could book an exit at a bar from before the signal existed. Every closed trade was re-graded against bars that actually printed.
evidence: exits corrected to a real price
engine.note: This moved the headline number against me. It is published anyway, because the earlier number was not real. Pre-correction data is kept in the repo rather than deleted.

engine.title: A first target must pay back the risk
engine.body: T1 was whichever structural level sat nearest the entry, with no distance test. One signal shipped a T1 worth 0.19R against its own stop, printed beside an R:R of 2.41 quoted off T2. T1 must now return at least 1R.

chess.title: Strategy: Open Files for Rooks
chess.body: Rooks need open files to be active. An open file has no pawns. A semi-open file has only enemy pawns. Double rooks on an open file (called 'Rooks on 7th') is a deadly battery. Strategy: open files by pawn trades, then occupy them immediately. Don't leave your rooks passive on the back rank.

wisdom.title: Financial Peace = Emotional Peace
wisdom.body: Money stress is the #1 relationship killer. Getting to AED 30K/month isn't just ambition — it's removing a major source of family stress. Every step toward financial stability is a step toward being a calmer, more present parent and partner. The job hunt matters. The income matters. It's not selfish. It's foundational.

book.author: Stephen Covey
book.chapter: Begin With the End in Mind
book.lesson: Covey's second habit: all things are created twice — first in the mind, then in the physical world. Everything you build, achieve, or create begins as a mental blueprint. Most people let life happen to them rather than designing it deliberately. The exercise: write your own eulogy. What do you want people to say about you as a parent, partner, professional, community member? That vision becomes your personal mission statement. Every decision then gets filtered through it: does this action align with the person I'm trying to become? This is the difference between living by design and living by default.
book.key_quote: If you don't define success for yourself, you'll spend your life achieving someone else's definition of it.
book.action: Write 3 sentences about the legacy you want to leave as a father and as a finance professional. Read them every morning this week.
crux: Character ethic beats personality ethic. Techniques without character are manipulation.
Paradigms determine what you see. Change the map before optimising the route.
Habit 1 — Be Proactive: between stimulus and response is your freedom to choose.
Focus on your Circle of Influence, not your Circle of Concern. The first grows; the second drains.
Habit 2 — Begin with the End in Mind: write the personal mission statement, then live backwards from it.
Habit 3 — First Things First: Quadrant II (important, not urgent) is where effectiveness lives.
Urgency addiction disguises itself as productivity. Most of Quadrant I is neglected Quadrant II.
Habit 4 — Think Win/Win: scarcity thinking produces win/lose; abundance produces cooperation.
Habit 5 — Seek First to Understand, Then to Be Understood. Diagnose before prescribing.
Empathic listening is the highest-leverage communication skill and almost nobody does it.
Habit 6 — Synergise: 1+1 can equal 3 when differences are valued rather than tolerated.
Habit 7 — Sharpen the Saw: renew physical, mental, social/emotional, spiritual capacity.
P/PC balance: production versus production capability. Killing the goose for the eggs.
The Emotional Bank Account — trust accumulates through deposits and is spent by withdrawals.
learnings: Effectiveness is a private victory before it is a public one.
Quadrant II work never announces itself. You must schedule it.
Most communication failures are prescription before diagnosis.
Renewal is not a reward for finishing. It is the capacity to finish.
examples: Viktor Frankl in the camps: everything removed except the choice of response. The origin of Habit 1.
Covey's funeral exercise — what four speakers would say about you — reframes goals from achievement to character.
The father who lists his son's faults and cannot understand why the son won't talk. Diagnosis skipped entirely.
adapt: Circle of influence on the Meta case: control the caption process, not the platform's decision.
Quadrant II: the Dubai applications and the daughter's bedtime. Neither is urgent. Both decide the decade.
Sharpen the saw is not optional at 7 hours' sleep — it is what makes the analysis correct.
Emotional bank account at home: presence deposits daily. The balance is what carries the hard months.

interview_tech.q: Explain covenant headroom and how you monitor it.
interview_tech.a: Covenants are contractual ratios — typically net debt to EBITDA, interest cover, and sometimes minimum net worth — tested quarterly. Headroom is the distance between your forecast ratio and the limit. Monitor it forward, not backward: run the covenant calculation inside the rolling forecast so you see a breach two quarters out while you can still act. Post-IFRS 16, check whether the definitions are frozen GAAP or current GAAP — lease liabilities entering net debt has breached covenants that had nothing to do with performance.

interview_tech.q: What controls matter most in a 60-store retail environment?
interview_tech.a: Rank by exposure. Cash and tender reconciliation daily at store level with independent review; goods receiving matched three-way to purchase order and invoice, because that is where margin leaks; inventory counts on a rolling cycle rather than one annual heroic count; markdown authorisation limits by role; and user access in the ERP reviewed quarterly, especially for leavers. Segregation of duties is hardest at small stores — compensate with detective controls and exception reporting rather than pretending it exists.

interview_soft.q: How would your team describe your management style?
interview_soft.a: Answer with evidence rather than adjectives. 'They would say I am specific — I give the number I expect and the date, and I do not change it quietly. They would also say I go into detail on their work more than some managers, which is useful when they are learning and irritating when they are not, so I have had to learn where to stop.' Naming the downside of your own style is what makes the strength believable.

interview_soft.q: How do you handle stress and long hours during close or audit?
interview_soft.a: They are checking sustainability, not stoicism. Do not claim you thrive on pressure. Give the operating answer: what you do to make the peak smaller (moving work out of the close), how you protect the team (rotating the worst shifts, protecting recovery time after), and what you personally do that is non-negotiable. Having a young child is relevant here and worth saying — it reads as someone with real boundaries rather than someone who has not been tested yet.

cfo_field.q: Read the cash flow statement first. Always.
cfo_field.a: P&L is an opinion, cash is a fact. Open any set of accounts at the cash flow statement, compare operating cash flow to EBITDA over three years, and look at the gap. A business converting 90%+ of EBITDA to operating cash is real. One converting 50% has its profit sitting in working capital or is capitalising something it should be expensing. That one ratio finds more problems than any variance pack.
cfo_field.who: The first thing to check, every time

cfo_field.q: Scenario planning beats a single budget, and costs less than it sounds.
cfo_field.a: Three cases — base, downside, upside — with the two or three variables that actually move the outcome, not thirty. In retail that is usually like-for-like growth, gross margin, and rent renewals. The value is not the numbers; it is that the board has already discussed the downside before it arrives, so the conversation when it does is about the response rather than about whether it is happening.

lichess_games.analysis: Focus on early king safety: after 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 d6, develop knights before pushing ...f6; avoid moving the g‑pawn—your king stayed exposed, leading to the mate at move 37. Strengthen pawn structure and castle promptly.

lichess_summary.session_summary: AKK_010’s single loss shows a complete collapse against even modest opposition—your opening choices are either nonexistent or disastrously mis‑played, leaving you with no viable middle‑game plans. Stop relying on “guesswork” and adopt a concrete, tested repertoire (e.g., 1.e4 C20 Italian Game or 1.d4 D00 Queen’s Gambit) and drill the first ten moves until they’re second nature. From now on, review every game with a computer, annotate every mistake, and spend at least one hour daily on forced‑mate puzzles to rebuild tactical vision before you even think about playing again.
